caption:
Amazon, Google, Microsoft, and Meta signed $1.5T in AI data center leases, many for buildings not yet built. The total tab hits $7 trillion by 2030. Swipe to see what it means for you. 📡

Everyone assumed AI was purely software with no physical footprint, four companies signed over $1.5 trillion in data center leases since the AI boom began, the US count of large-scale data centers is projected to triple from 90 to 280 by 2030, total industry spend is expected to hit $7 trillion which is roughly Japan's entire annual economy, power grids and electricity costs will feel the new demand first, and most businesses still haven't figured out how to use the AI those buildings will run.

The AI revolution isn't invisible code. It's the fastest physical infrastructure build in a generation, already underway across the US. Power grids, land prices, and electricity costs sit downstream of this spending. The companies writing the checks aren't even certain AI demand will hold at the level they need. They're paying for a future they're betting on, not one they've confirmed. Running a business? DM us "AI" and we'll show you what this could do for yours.

Sources: The Kobeissi Letter on X
